one_liner: Header-only branchless integer-to-ASCII conversion, ~7-9x faster than sprintf/MSVC _itoa, ~1.6-1.8x vs {fmt}.
what_it_does: Converts signed and unsigned integers (8/16/32/64-bit) to decimal ASCII text into a caller-supplied buffer. The API is `char* to_text_from_integer(char* buf, T n)`: it returns a pointer just past the last digit written, does not null-terminate, and performs no bounds checking or error reporting, so it is not a drop-in for std::to_chars despite the similar shape. The function is a template, so the compiler specializes the branch structure and constants per integer type and size.
how_it_is_fast: Uses a per-digit-length unrolled code path chosen by a small binary-search branch tree on the number's decimal length, so short numbers take fewer branches than long ones instead of looping once per digit. Digits are produced two at a time via fixed-point multiply-shift arithmetic against a 100-entry '00'-'99' ASCII lookup table, avoiding per-digit division; only one true integer divide is used, to split 64-bit values into two 8-digit halves. The fixed-point constants follow the classic multiply-by-2^k/10^n itoa trick, refined using the mathematical analysis in dragonbox author Junekey Jeon's write-up, which removed a redundant addition.
when_to_use: Hot paths that serialize many plain base-10 integers to text (logging, JSON/CSV encoders, protocol formatting) on MSVC, clang, or gcc
Fixed 8/16/32/64-bit integer types where you control the destination buffer size and will add the null terminator yourself
Workloads with uniform or skewed digit-length distributions (IDs, counters) where branch-prediction-unfriendly random lengths matter
Need a single self-contained, zero-dependency header (not even <cstdint>) that works from C++11 up, easy to vendor
You're comfortable auditing/patching abandonware yourself rather than depending on upstream maintenance
when_not_to_use: Need floating-point-to-string conversion; integers only, no float/double support at all
Need std::to_chars' API contract: error_code / bool success return, [first,last) bounds-checked span; this header has neither

Need guaranteed-correct output without your own verification: the repo has shipped at least two silent, large-magnitude correctness bugs on big 64-bit inputs (issues #12, #18), both fixed only because users noticed
Want zero-padding or fixed-point/decimal formatting; explicitly requested in issue #15 and not implemented
Need a plain-C API; this is C++ template code with no official C binding (issue #10 still open, unresolved)

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (compiles on clang, MSVC, and gcc per README)
integration.platforms: any (no architecture-specific intrinsics in the header; author's benchmarks are x86/x64 Windows/VC2019)
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly, but the function only reads compile-time constexpr tables and writes to the caller-supplied buffer, so concurrent calls with distinct buffers are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same 'write digits, return end pointer' shape as std::to_chars, but no error_code, no bounds checking against a span, and no automatic null termination

gotchas: Output is not null-terminated; caller must write '\0' at the returned pointer (see test/main.cpp's to_string wrappers)
No bounds checking: caller must size the buffer for the worst case (up to 20 digits + sign for 64-bit) or risk a buffer overflow

History of silent large-magnitude correctness bugs on 64-bit inputs (issue #12: off by 10,000,000 on a 19-digit value; issue #18: wrong values near a specific 11-digit range), both fixed before the final 2022-11-24 commit but with no maintainer left to catch new regressions

Repo contains multiple header variants (include/itoa/jeaiii_to_text.h is current; itoa/to_text_from_integer.h and itoa/int_to_chars_jeaiii.h are older macro-based versions) — include the one under include/itoa/, not the legacy ones
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick jeaiii/itoa over CharConv.h (rigtorp) or c4core when you want the smallest possible single header with zero includes and don't need from_chars/parsing or float formatting. Pick c4core or Boost.Charconv instead when you need a maintained, std::to_chars/from_chars-compatible API with float support and bounds-checked spans.
verified_claims_summary: Author-run release-mode benchmark (Visual C++ 2019, win64, hardware unstated) using jeaiii's fork of miloyip/itoa-benchmark shows, on uniform-random-digit-length inputs, u32toa at 20.5 cycles vs sprintf's 160.5 and MSVC _ui64toa's 174.5 (~8x), and vs {fmt}'s 33.5 (~1.6x); u64toa is 32.75 cycles vs sprintf's 226.75 and MSVC's 312 (~7-9x), and vs {fmt}'s 58 (~1.8x). A separate debug-built Google Benchmark on godbolt, which the author explicitly disclaims as not a good benchmark, shows 10.2ns vs {fmt}'s 16.6ns. No comparison against std::to_chars is published anywhere in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned since its last commit on 2022-11-24 with no tagged releases; MIT-licensed and small enough (~200-line single header) to vendor and patch yourself, but its history of correctness bugs on large 64-bit values means you should add your own exhaustive round-trip test before trusting it in production.
